findings.reason: a node dispatched on this section either blocks on its grant or duplicates §20's resolver in a caller, and either way the plan needs `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py` added to the write paths plus an ordering behind §20.
findings.text: §21's deliverable says the persisted directive environment "passes the backend name", but the function that composes it, `_persisted_worker_environment` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:670`), is not in the section's write paths: `dispatch.py:3343` only calls it, and it is the one place that forwards the overlay to `launch_search_path` (`dispatch_launch.py:696`), so the backend name cannot reach the PATH from `dispatch.py` without a signature change in a file §21 does not grant; and the section is declared `implementable` although `launch_search_path` (`dispatch_launch.py:609`) takes no declared-path input today, which is what §20 adds and whose grant is the disjoint set `dispatch_launch.py`, `_backends.py`, `_flight_schema.py`.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/flight.py:2349` holds `located = shutil.which(command)` exactly and the `"not on PATH"` detail is at :2370; `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` "near line 3282" resolves to the `_persisted_worker_environment` call at :3343, whose named symbol removes the 61-line drift as a hazard.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §21 names two cases with a stub backend on a directory absent from PATH, two negative controls that are real mutations (drop the backend name from the persisted environment; restore bare `shutil.which`), and a base-revision delta for the importing test files.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the arms log "under the run directory", which is the durable crew run path, and the new test file is created in `tests/`; nothing in the done-when names a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `test_every_backend_reader_searches_the_declared_path.py` names the capability, and the only identifier-shaped citation in the prose (`r-20261108T202504141562`) is run evidence, not code, a symbol or a comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §21's stated cause matches the cited review exactly (that run's `outside_scope` records `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3282` and `reckon/flight.py:2349` with the same two mechanisms), and both targets are on real production paths: `_persisted_worker_environment` is called at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3343` and `probe_availability` is called at `reckon/flight.py:2720` and `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:619`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the section names one property (every backend reader resolves a backend command the way the launch does), the two readers are instances of it, and one new test file carries the single verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §21's write paths (`docs/plans/a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker.html:1036`) grant `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` and `reckon/flight.py`, but the function its first deliverable changes, `_persisted_worker_environment`, is defined in `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:670`; the section is also declared `implementable` although its mechanism only exists after §20 lands.
